title: Twenty-sixth Dynasty of Egypt
capsule: The Twenty-sixth Dynasty (664–525 BCE), the Saite Period named for its capital Sais in the western Nile Delta, was founded by Psamtik I (664–610 BCE), who expelled the Assyrian-backed garrisons and reunified Egypt after a century of Nubian and Assyrian domination. Under Psamtik I and his successors — Necho II (610–595), who cut the first Suez canal and defeated Josiah of Judah at Megiddo; Psamtik II (595–589); Apries (589–570); and Amasis (570–526), who opened Egypt to Greek commerce and defeated a Babylonian naval incursion — the dynasty sustained a deliberate cultural renaissance modeled on Old Kingdom precedents. The dynasty ended in 525 BCE when Cambyses II of Persia defeated Psamtik III at the Battle of Pelusium and incorporated Egypt into the Achaemenid Empire as a satrapy, initiating the Twenty-seventh Dynasty.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The dynasty's territorial extent is well documented by Egyptian monuments, Herodotus, and Babylonian chronicles; the dataset from/to dates (−615/−500) are Cliopatria attestation windows that differ slightly from the canonical 664–525 BCE.
